prompt: In mousePressed, branch on e.getButton() so the left button adds a dot, the right button undoes the newest one (harmlessly when empty) and the middle button clears them all.
explanation: One MouseEvent carries which physical button caused it, so a single mousePressed method can drive three different commands by comparing e.getButton() with MouseEvent.BUTTON1, BUTTON2 and BUTTON3. The undo branch shows the usual defensive habit for list-backed state: check isEmpty() before removing at size() - 1, otherwise an eager right-click throws IndexOutOfBoundsException. Refreshing the label after the branch means it is updated exactly once no matter which button was pressed.
hints: MouseEvent.BUTTON1, BUTTON2 and BUTTON3 are plain int constants -- compare them with == against e.getButton().
The newest element of a List is at index size() - 1, and that expression is only valid when the list is not empty.
Update the dots label once, after the branching, so every path keeps it correct.
